design_rationale: Explicit computer-generated random allocation of 80 ICU post-cardiac-surgery patients 1:1:2 to EPO 20,000 IU, EPO 40,000 IU, or saline placebo, with allocation envelopes and double blinding; registered as NCT00676234.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation sequence was computer-generated with 1:1:2 ratio, concealed in envelopes prepared by an independent quality-of-care unit and administered by a nurse not involved in assessment, and baseline characteristics (age, sex, comorbidity, creatinine, uNGAL) did not differ between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "A randomization code was generated by a computer 1:1:2 and envelopes with allocation were prepared by the quality of care unit. A nurse from the Nephrology Unit opened the envelopes and prepared the syringes for injection."

domain_judgments.rationale: Patients and investigators/carers were blinded, the intervention was a single intravenous dose with a matched saline placebo so deviations were unlikely, and no participants were excluded after randomization (all randomized patients analysed in their allocated group).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Investigators and patients were blinded to the treatment... No patient was excluded after randomization."

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were essentially complete: only one of 80 patients lacked the 48-h biological sampling (transferred to another hospital) and his clinical status was ascertained, a proportion too small to bias results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Only 1 patient was transferred in another hospital at 48 h. Although we could not have the complete biological follow-up, we could have the information that he did not develop AKI and was alive."

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were objective laboratory biomarkers (uNGAL by ELISA, creatinine, cystatin C, cytokines) measured identically and batched in all groups under blinded conditions, minimizing assessor influence; the only caveat is absence of pre-surgical baseline uNGAL values, acknowledged by the authors but affecting groups equally.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "All samples for NGAL and cytokines measures were processed at the same time."

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered with a clearly stated primary outcome that was reported, but no protocol/analysis plan is available and the reported analyses include an apparently post-hoc pooling of the two EPO dose arms plus numerous additional comparisons (multiple biomarkers, time points, subgroups by AKI and mortality) without a pre-specified analysis strategy.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "We pooled the two EPO doses and confirmed that r-HuEPO did not significantly modify uNGAL median levels between 48 hours and randomization"

overall_summary: Allocation was computer-randomized and concealed, blinding was maintained, outcome data were virtually complete, and outcomes were objective laboratory measures (all low risk). Overall judgment of "some concerns" is driven solely by Domain 5: absence of an available protocol/pre-specified analysis plan combined with post-hoc pooling of dose arms and many additional biomarker/subgroup comparisons; the study is also acknowledged to be underpowered, which affects precision rather than bias.

design_rationale: The paper explicitly describes a prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial with 1:1 blocked randomization and allocation via sealed envelopes ("Treatment assignment among the two groups was determined by blocked randomization").

domain_judgments.rationale: Blocked 1:1 randomization with allocation concealed in sealed envelopes opened by nurses not involved in the study, and baseline demographic, comorbidity, renal and intra-operative variables were statistically comparable between groups (all p > 0.05), although the envelopes are not described as opaque/sequentially numbered.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Treatment assignment among the two groups was determined by blocked randomization. After recruitment, three days before the operation, sealed envelopes containing the allocation group were opened by nurses who did not participate in the study."

domain_judgments.rationale: Patients, investigators and outcome assessors were blinded with identical placebo syringes, no deviations from the intended regimen were reported, and the two post-randomization exclusions (one per arm, before receiving treatment) are balanced and unlikely to distort the effect estimate, though a strict intention-to-treat analysis is not explicitly stated.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Pairs of identical 0.3 ml syringes containing either rHuEPO (5,000 U, Recormon, Roche) or saline were prepared and stored... Patients and investigators were also blinded to group assignment."

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data appear available for all 100 treated patients (50 per group) with only two exclusions before treatment (one per arm) clearly documented in the CONSORT-style flow diagram, so missingness is minimal and balanced.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "One patient in the rHuEPO and one from the placebo group were excluded because of the lack of medical treatment and a CABG cancelation. Consequently, 100 patients received their assigned treatments to the placebo (n = 50) or rHuEPO (n = 50) group."

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome (KDIGO-defined AKI from serum creatinine) is objective, measured identically in a single hospital laboratory in both arms, and NGAL assays were performed in duplicate in a blinded fashion with assessors unaware of allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "All laboratory parameters were performed in a single, hospital-based laboratory using standard methods... The measurements were made in duplicate and in a blinded fashion."

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered (NCT01066351) with pre-specified primary and secondary endpoints, but recruitment was stopped early at 50 per group (below the pre-calculated 65 per group) apparently because significance had been reached, which raises concern about analysis/stopping-driven reporting; additionally the AKI definition was applied using KDIGO 2012 criteria published after the 2010–2011 trial period and multiple subgroup/time-point NGAL analyses are reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "the sample size in each group was 65 patients. However, the statistic significant between both groups become since the population size in each group was 50 patients. Therefore, a total of 100 patients were randomized in the present study."

overall_summary: Randomization, blinding, follow-up completeness and objective, blinded outcome measurement were all well handled (low risk in D1–D4). Overall judgment of "some concerns" is driven by D5: the trial was terminated early at a smaller sample than pre-planned because statistical significance had been achieved, the outcome definition used criteria published after the trial, and multiple time-point/subgroup analyses were reported, raising the possibility of selective reporting.

design_rationale: Explicit randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial with central web-based allocation stratified by sex, age, center and cancer site.

domain_judgments.rationale: Central internet-based stratified randomization performed by independent secretaries ensured concealment, and baseline characteristics were similar between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Randomization to study treatment was performed by authorized secretaries via an Internet homepage ... and was stratified by sex, age ..., center and cancer localization. Participants and investigators were unaware of treatment allocation at all times."

domain_judgments.rationale: Double-blinded with identical-appearing placebo (isotonic saline) produced/blinded by the manufacturer, codes never broken, and analysis stated to be intention-to-treat per a pre-established plan.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Code-breaking sheets for emergency use were available but were never used." ... "Data were entered before treatment codes were broken and analyzed on an intent-to-treat basis according to a preestablished analysis plan."

domain_judgments.rationale: Only 151 of 202 randomized patients (≈75%) were in the efficacy-valid population, with post-randomization exclusions (12 DA vs 18 placebo) and 17 dropouts plus missing day-7 ergometer tests for abdominoperineal resections; reasons appear largely unrelated to treatment but no sensitivity analysis of missingness is reported despite the ITT claim.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "In total, 221 patients were enrolled into the study, of whom 202 patients were randomized and 151 completed the study (efficacy-valid population)."

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were assessed with standardized instrumented measures (cycle ergometer heart rate, force platform sway, dynamometer strength) and validated questionnaires, applied identically at fixed time points with both patients and investigators blinded.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Participants and investigators were unaware of treatment allocation at all times."

domain_judgments.rationale: A pre-established analysis plan and a clearly stated primary outcome are described, but there is no trial-registration reference, several co-primary physical performance outcomes are reported, and no correction for multiple testing was made, leaving some scope for selective emphasis (e.g., the single positive work-capacity result).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "No correction for multiple testing was made."

overall_summary: Allocation, blinding and outcome measurement were strong, but roughly a quarter of randomized patients were excluded or dropped out without sensitivity analyses, and multiple primary outcomes were analyzed without multiplicity correction or a cited registration, yielding an overall judgment of some concerns.

design_rationale: The paper explicitly describes a prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial with a computer/center-generated randomization code list (block size two, stratified by SCr and CPB use) and internet-based 1:1 allocation to EPO or saline.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation sequence was centrally generated and stratified, concealment was ensured by internet-based central allocation with a coordinator preparing identical syringes, and baseline characteristics were broadly comparable (minor imbalances in valve surgery and CPB use are consistent with chance in a small trial).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "A randomization code list with a block size of two was generated by Medical Research Collaborating Center Seoul National University Hospital... Treatments were allocated to patients through the Internet in accordance with the predefined randomization list (1:1 ratio for EPO or placebo group)."

domain_judgments.rationale: Double blinding with matched saline placebo given as a single pre-operative intravenous bolus makes performance deviations unlikely, and all 71 randomized patients received their assigned intervention and were analyzed as allocated.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Patients, healthcare clinicians, and investigators were blinded to treatment assignment."

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data appear available for all randomized participants, with no reported loss to follow-up (only 1 in-hospital death, in the placebo group).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "71 patients were randomized to receive EPO (n = 36) or saline (n = 35) and completed this trial."

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome is an objective laboratory-based definition (≥50% SCr rise) measured identically and at fixed times in both arms by blinded personnel, so assessor knowledge could not plausibly bias it.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "SCr was measured using modified Jaffé method on a Toshiba 200FR Analyzer (Toshiba, Tokyo, Japan). The analytical coef ficient of variation of this assay is 3.01%."

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered and the primary endpoint pre-specified, but registration occurred after enrollment began (Sept 2006 vs. NCT registered 2008), no protocol/analysis plan is available for inspection, no sample size calculation is given, and multiple outcome operationalizations (absolute and relative SCr/eGFR changes at three time points plus CKD/non-CKD subgroups) were reported, leaving some scope for selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "This trial was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (www.clinicaltrial.gov), No. NCT 00654992."

overall_summary: This double-blind, centrally randomized placebo-controlled pilot trial had sound allocation concealment, complete outcome data, and an objective laboratory-defined primary outcome, but concerns remain about selective reporting given retrospective-appearing registration, absence of an available protocol/power calculation, and multiple reported outcome operationalizations and subgroup analyses in a very small sample. Overall risk is therefore 'some concerns', driven by domain 5.

design_rationale: Explicit random allocation is described: 74 anemic patients were "randomly allocated to either the rHuEPO or the control group in a 1:1 ratio by means of computer-generated random numbers," in a prospective, single-blinded, parallel-arm controlled trial.

domain_judgments.rationale: Computer-generated random numbers were used with allocation performed by a ward physician not involved in the trial, and baseline demographics, comorbidities and EuroSCORE were similar between groups (only a nonsignificant β-blocker imbalance, which was adjusted for).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Patients were randomly allocated to either the rHuEPO or the control group in a 1:1 ratio by means of computer-generated random numbers. A ward physician not involved in the current trial performed randomization and assignment."

domain_judgments.rationale: Surgeons/anesthesiologists managing patients and transfusion were blinded and all 74 randomized patients were analyzed, but the trial was only single-blinded (the administering ward physician knew allocation), controls received saline without iron so the comparison is co-intervention-confounded (EPO+iron vs. nothing), and no explicit placebo for iron was used.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Medications were prepared and administered by a ward physician recognizing the patient’s group but not involved in the current study, whereas the surgeon and anesthesiologist involved in the study and patient management were blinded to the patients’ groups until the end of the study."

domain_judgments.rationale: Complete primary-outcome data were available for all 74 randomized patients, although a few secondary outcomes (AKI, atrial fibrillation) had small denominators (e.g., 35/37, 30/37) without explanation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "VHS could be performed as planned in all patients, and complete data sets from the 74 patients were analyzed without any missing data."

domain_judgments.rationale: Transfusion requirement is an objective, protocol-driven outcome with predefined hemoglobin triggers applied identically in both groups, and clinicians deciding transfusion were blinded to allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Hemoglobin concentration less than 7 mg/dl during CPB, and less than 8 mg/dl after CPB and postoperatively, were used as transfusion thresholds."

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary and secondary endpoints and a prospective sample-size calculation are clearly stated and an independent data monitoring board reviewed interim data, but no trial registration number or pre-specified analysis plan is cited, and post hoc adjusted analyses (e.g., for β-blocker use) plus multiple transfusion operationalizations and time windows leave some selective-reporting risk.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Therefore, we also adjusted for -blocker use in our between-group comparisons of reticulocyte response over time using mixed linear model assessment; similar results were observed as in our presented analyses."

overall_summary: Randomization, outcome completeness and objective protocol-driven transfusion outcome assessment were well handled, but the trial was only single-blinded with a saline control lacking iron co-intervention (making the contrast EPO+iron vs. nothing), and no prospective registration/analysis plan is reported alongside post hoc adjusted analyses. These issues in D2 and D5 yield an overall judgment of some concerns.

design_rationale: This is a pre-planned sub-study of the EPO-TBI double-blind randomized controlled trial in which patients "were randomized to weekly EPO (40 000 units) or placebo (0.9% sodium chloride) subcutaneously", with trial registration (NCT00987454); the EPO vs placebo comparison for AKI outcomes is therefore assessed with RoB 2.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation sequence generation and concealment are not described within this report (only cross-referenced to the parent trial), and no baseline comparison of EPO vs placebo groups is presented in this sub-study, although the parent trial was a registered double-blind placebo-controlled RCT so serious problems are unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The randomization process and administration of drug has been described previously.

domain_judgments.rationale: The parent trial was double-blind with a matched saline placebo, all randomized patients except three who withdrew consent were analyzed (603/606, effectively intention-to-treat), and no important deviations are reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Enrolled patients received either weekly doses of 40 000 IU of subcutaneous epoetin alfa (Eprex Janssen‐Cilag Pty Ltd, Titusville, NJ, USA) or placebo (0.9% sodium chloride).

domain_judgments.rationale: Creatinine-based outcome data were available for nearly all randomized patients (603/606), but urinary-output data were restricted to 7 days and no post-ICU renal data were collected, and completeness of daily creatinine/UO records per arm is not quantified.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Data on urinary output according to the KDIGO stages were only available during the first 7 days of ICU care.

domain_judgments.rationale: AKI was defined by objective, standard KDIGO criteria using prospectively recorded laboratory values applied identically in both blinded arms, and 6-month neurological outcome was assessed by a blinded assessor, so assessor knowledge is unlikely to bias measurement.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Serum creatinine was prospectively recorded daily until ICU discharge and urine output during the first 7 days.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although the sub-study protocol and a sample size calculation are reported, multiple AKI operationalizations (creatinine-only over whole ICU stay, creatinine+UO at 7 days, AKI-free days, day-3 landmark models) and partly data-driven covariate selection (P<0.1 in univariate analysis) create scope for selective reporting; the editorial comment also labels it a "post-hoc subgroup analysis," and reported EPO hazard ratios for time to AKI are inconsistent between the abstract (HR 1.08) and results (HR 0.99/0.9).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The EPO‐AKI sub‐study was a pre‐planned study and the protocol (a part of the original EPO‐AKI protocol) is included in the Supplementary Materials.

overall_summary: The EPO vs placebo comparison derives from a large, registered, double-blind, placebo-controlled multicentre RCT with objective KDIGO outcomes, giving low risk for intervention delivery and outcome measurement. Overall risk is "some concerns" because randomization details are only cross-referenced (with no arm-level baseline data shown), urinary-output/renal data were incomplete beyond 7 days, and the multiplicity of AKI definitions and analyses (with inconsistent reported hazard ratios) raises the possibility of selective result reporting in this underpowered sub-study.

design_rationale: Patients were explicitly randomly allocated 1:1 to EPO or control using a computer-generated random code in a double-blind, placebo (saline)-controlled trial registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT01758861).

domain_judgments.rationale: A computer-generated random sequence was used and baseline characteristics were broadly similar, but the mechanism of allocation concealment is not explicitly described and there was a notable (though non-significant) imbalance in diabetes mellitus (16% vs 33%, P = 0.060), a factor the authors themselves acknowledge may modify EPO's tissue-protective effect.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Patients were randomly allocated to either the EPO or control group in a 1:1 ratio according to simple randomization using a computer-generated random code." ... "Second, more patients had DM in the EPO group, although these results were not statistically significant."

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was double-blind with an identical-volume saline placebo prepared by a nurse not otherwise involved in the study, perioperative care was protocolized and comparable between groups (CPB time, fluids, transfusion, vasopressors), and all randomized patients were analyzed as allocated.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Patients in the control group received an equal volume of normal saline at the same time point. Medications were prepared by a nurse who knew the patient's group assignment but was not involved in the study."

domain_judgments.rationale: No participants were lost after allocation, so the primary outcome (AKI) was available for all 98 randomized patients; the biomarker substudy was pre-planned in a randomly selected subset of 18 per group rather than representing attrition.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "A total of ninety-eight patients were randomized to receive EPO (n = 49) or normal saline (n = 49), and no patient was dropped out after group allocation (Figure 1)."

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome was an objective, standardized laboratory-based definition (AKIN serum creatinine criteria) supplemented by objective assay-based biomarkers (cystatin C, NGAL, IL-6, MPO), measured identically and at identical time points in both groups under double-blind conditions, leaving little scope for assessor influence.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The primary endpoint of interest was incidence of AKI, which was diagnosed according to the Acute Kidney Injury Network (AKIN) criteria (absolute increase in the sCr concentration ≥0.3 mg/dL from baseline or ≥50% increase in the sCr concentration within 48 hours after operation)"

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered with a clearly pre-specified primary endpoint and an a priori sample-size calculation, but the registration record is not available for comparison against the reported outcomes, multiple secondary biomarker outcomes and time points were analyzed, and several supportive analyses are reported only as "data not shown" (hemodynamics, non-DM subgroup, Voluven–creatinine association), indicating some unreported/selectively presented analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "There were no differences in mean blood glucose levels, renal biomarkers and the incidence of AKI between the groups even in patients without DM (data not shown)."

overall_summary: This registered, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial was well conducted with complete outcome data, objective blinded outcome measurement, and no deviations from intended interventions. Overall judgment of "some concerns" is driven by incompletely described allocation concealment with a borderline baseline imbalance in diabetes (D1) and by unverifiable pre-specification plus several post hoc analyses reported only as "data not shown" (D5); the study was also underpowered because observed AKI incidence was lower than assumed.

design_rationale: The record is a conference abstract supplement (ISICEM 2014) whose constituent studies are audits, before-after quality-improvement projects, retrospective/prospective cohorts, surveys and literature reviews (e.g., "We audited the daily infusion charts ... A month later the audit process was repeated"; "A retrospective review ..."); nowhere is random allocation of participants/units to conditions described, so it cannot be classified as randomized.

domain_judgments.rationale: Comparisons are uncontrolled before-after or between-unit contrasts with no adjustment for secular trends, case-mix or co-interventions (e.g., prescribing audit of 129 vs 111 prescriptions a month apart; VAP bundle 2011 vs a later 3-month period), and even where confounders are discussed they are not systematically measured.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "We assessed 129 prescriptions in the fi rst round, and 111 after intervention, demonstrating a 70% improvement in safe prescribing."

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias in selection of participants into the study
domain_judgments.rationale: Participants/records were convenience samples from single units during arbitrary audit windows with no described eligibility or consecutive-enrolment criteria, and "spot checks" risk selecting periods/charts related to both the intervention and the outcome.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "We audited the daily infusion charts of all patients in three separate spot checks, over 1 week."

domain_judgments.rationale: The interventions (standardised prescription sticker plus education, protocol plus education, bundle redesign) are defined by time period and so classification is unlikely to be misassigned, but the content, dose and fidelity of the multifaceted interventions are only superficially described in abstract form.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "New procedures were introduced, which included a standardised prescription sticker, with common, preprinted, infusion prescriptions on (noradrenaline, propofol, and so forth), and education on using the new prescription stickers."

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias due to deviations from intended interventions
domain_judgments.rationale: Staff were necessarily aware of the audit and the newly introduced tools/protocols, creating strong potential for Hawthorne effects and co-interventions, and no fidelity monitoring or intention-to-treat-style analysis is reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "After the fi rst audit period a simple education programme was delivered. We also introduced a departmental protocol for the prevention and management of inadvertent hypothermia. Six months later we re-audited our practice."

domain_judgments.rationale: No accounting of missing charts, non-responders or incomplete records is provided for most abstracts, and where incompleteness is acknowledged it is substantial and unaddressed (e.g., missing essential booking data, missing autopsy reports, questionnaire non-response).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "There were 105 handwritten bookings over 10 months, several missing essential data."

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes (e.g., "best practice criteria" compliance, bundle compliance, documented interventions) were assessed by unblinded local staff who delivered the intervention, using documentation-based measures whose rigour may itself have changed with the new forms/stickers; no inter-rater reliability or blinded assessment is reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Only 24% of prescriptions initially fulfi lled best practice criteria, improving to 94% afterwards."

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias in selection of the reported result
domain_judgments.rationale: There is no protocol or pre-registration, multiple outcome measures and subgroup comparisons are reported selectively in a brief abstract format (with some figures/tables referenced but not shown), and favourable results are emphasised without a pre-specified primary outcome or correction for multiplicity.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "With a small, cost-ef ective intervention (£20 for 6,200 stickers), we improved prescribing accuracy, and thus patient safety in intensive care."

overall_summary: This record is a conference abstract supplement comprising uncontrolled before-after audits, retrospective record reviews and surveys with no randomization, no confounder adjustment, unblinded outcome ascertainment by the same staff delivering the interventions, and no protocol or pre-specified outcomes. Multiple domains (confounding, selection, deviations, missing data, outcome measurement, selective reporting) are at serious risk, so the overall judgment is serious risk of bias; the abstract format also precludes verification of key methodological details.

design_rationale: The data come from the Epo-ACR-02 multicentre randomized controlled trial in which "patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to the intervention or to the control group" with stratification by site; this report is a post hoc analysis of a single-centre subset of that randomized population, so RoB 2 applies (with attention to the post hoc subsetting).

domain_judgments.rationale: Randomization with site stratification was performed in the parent trial and baseline characteristics were similar, but no details on sequence generation or allocation concealment are given in this report, and the analysed sample is a post-randomization single-centre subset with further exclusions (CKD, early deaths), leaving some residual uncertainty (e.g. SAPS 2 P=0.06, age imbalance).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "After being screened for eligibility, patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to the intervention or to the control group. Intervention assignments were stratified by site."

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was open-label with no placebo, so treating clinicians knew allocation and could have altered co-interventions influencing AKI definition (e.g. RRT initiation, fluid/diuretic management), although adherence to the Epo schedule was high (89–97%) and ICU management appeared balanced; it is also unclear whether analysis was strictly intention-to-treat since early deaths and CKD patients were excluded post hoc.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "the Epo-ACR-02 study was an open-label trial"; "In the control group, patients received standard care without any Epo medication."

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary Day-2 outcome was available in 155/162 (~96%) and imputation rules were prespecified, but secondary endpoints (notably Day-28 eGFR, available in only 24 of 32 survivors) had substantial missingness and very high mortality attrition, with results reported only in those alive.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "since this study is a post hoc analysis, data concerning survival and renal function at Day 28 have been collected retrospectively, and thus some data were missing"; "Among the 32 patients with AKI at Day 2 still alive at Day 28, Day 28 creatinine was available in 24."

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome ascertainment used objective laboratory criteria (KDIGO) applied identically in both arms, but baseline creatinine was imputed rather than measured and components (urine output, RRT initiation) are clinician-dependent in an unblinded trial; sensitivity analyses using admission creatinine gave similar results, mitigating concern.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "to assess the pre-CA creatinine, we used a back-calculated creatinine through the MDRD equation assuming a 75 mL/min/1.73 m2 eGFR for every patient, whereas their anterior renal function was unknown... it could have created a bias in the proportion of AKI at Day 2."

domain_judgments.rationale: This is an explicitly post hoc, unregistered exploratory analysis restricted to one centre, with the AKI endpoint operationalized in many alternative ways (KDIGO 2–3, creatinine-only, urine output, admission vs back-calculated baseline, Day 2 vs Day 7, multiple timepoints) and no pre-specified analysis plan for these renal outcomes, creating high potential for selective reporting of results and analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "We therefore aimed to explore, post hoc, in a subgroup of the Epo-ACR-02 trial population, whether there are any renoprotective effects of Epo therapy"

overall_summary: Although derived from a randomized trial with balanced baseline characteristics and objective laboratory outcomes, this is an unregistered, exploratory post hoc single-centre subgroup analysis with multiple alternative outcome definitions and no pre-specified analysis plan, yielding high risk in the selective-reporting domain. Open-label design, imputed baseline creatinine and substantial missing Day-28 renal data add further (some) concerns, so the overall judgment is high risk of bias.

design_rationale: The paper explicitly describes a double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in which an independent investigator performed computer-generated randomization to erythropoietin or saline control ("An independent investigator performed computer-generated randomization, enrolled patients, and assigned patients to the erythropoietin group or the control group").

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation was computer-generated and concealed via an independent investigator who prepared masked solutions, but there was a statistically significant baseline imbalance in sex (61% vs 41% male, p = 0.04) plus unstratified randomization with numerical imbalances in diagnosis and procedure type, raising some concern.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "An independent investigator performed computer-generated randomization, enrolled patients, and assigned patients to the erythropoietin group or the control group. He also prepared all drug solutions and provided them to the anesthesia practitioner." ... "Male 19 (61) | 12 (41) | 0.04" ... "randomization was not stratified on the basis of risk factors for AKI"

domain_judgments.rationale: Patients, clinicians and assessors were blinded to a single identical-volume bolus of drug or saline, co-interventions (fluids, transfusion, anesthesia protocol, surgical team) were standardized and comparable between groups, and no intervention deviations were reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The anesthetic administrator, surgeons, patients, outcome assessors, and data analysts were all blinded to patient allocations throughout the entire study."

domain_judgments.rationale: Six of 66 randomized patients (9%) were excluded from analysis and the text does not state the reasons or their group allocation, so the analysis was not intention-to-treat and the potential influence of these exclusions cannot be fully verified from the narrative.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Of the 66 patients enrolled, 60 patients were included in the final analysis (Fig 1)."

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome was an objective, standardized laboratory-based definition (RIFLE by serum creatinine/eGFR, plus serum NGAL) measured identically in both groups with blinded assessors, so measurement bias is unlikely despite omission of the urine-output criterion.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The primary outcome was the incidence of AKI according to the RIFLE criteria" ... "outcome assessors, and data analysts were all blinded to patient allocations"

domain_judgments.rationale: No trial registration number or pre-specified analysis plan is reported; although the primary AKI endpoint was clearly pre-specified with a power calculation, the highlighted positive findings come from numerous secondary hemodynamic/complication outcomes analysed without multiplicity adjustment, raising concern about selective emphasis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Cardiac complications after surgery were significantly lower ... and the incidence of prolonged vasopressor dependence was reduced in the erythropoietin group (Table 4)"

overall_summary: This double-blind, computer-randomized, placebo-controlled trial had strong blinding and objective, uniformly measured renal outcomes, but a significant baseline sex imbalance with unstratified randomization, 9% unexplained post-randomization exclusions (60/66 analysed, non-ITT), and absence of a stated registration/pre-specified analysis plan for the many secondary outcomes raise some concerns. No single domain reached high risk, so the overall judgment is "some concerns," with the positive secondary cardiac findings being the least reliable results.

design_rationale: Ancillary (REPaIReD) study of the PENUT trial, an explicitly described multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized clinical trial with 1:1 allocation to rhEpo vs placebo stratified by gestational age, multiple birth, and site.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants, families, and study personnel were blinded with placebo/sham injections, analyses were by randomized arm, and no interventions deviations affecting kidney outcomes were reported (only 18 of 941 enrolled excluded for early death/misenrollment).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Study personnel and families were still blinded to randomization groups at the follow-up visit."

domain_judgments.rationale: Stratified 1:1 randomization within a double-blind placebo-controlled trial with baseline characteristics well balanced (only one of many comparisons, delivery-room positive pressure, differed at P=.04, consistent with chance).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "participants were randomized to rhEpo vs placebo within 24 hours of birth. Randomization allocation was 1:1, with patients stratified by gestational age category, multiple births, and study site." ... "The treatment groups were well matched for demographic characteristics and protective perinatal therapies."

domain_judgments.rationale: For the 22-26 month outcomes, eGFR was available in only ~36%, ACR in ~47% and blood pressure in ~53% of randomized infants, with differential availability by arm (BP available 56.8% placebo vs 49.7% Epo, P=.044; lost to follow-up 3.2% vs 8.3%, P=.01) and demographic imbalance among those missing BP, so the key positive SBP finding could plausibly be driven by missingness (as the authors themselves concede); short-term AKI data, by contrast, were near complete.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Hypertension value available, n (%) 258 (56.8%) 233 (49.7%) .044" ... "we acknowledge that a large number of patients did not have kidney-related metrics measured at the 2-year cGA time point."

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome assessors were blinded and methods were standardized across arms, but clinically-driven, heterogeneous local SCr assays and non-gold-standard one-visit measures (spot ACR, two manual BP readings reported as the lowest) introduce measurement error, though non-differential by arm.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Each NICU measured SCr according to their institutional guidelines using the local laboratory methodology available (11 Jaffe, 8 enzymatic)." ... "the methods to capture kidney-related outcomes (eGFR, spot urine ACR, and one-time manual blood pressure measurements) are not gold-standard methods"

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary short-term outcome was pre-specified and the trial registered (NCT01378273), but many long-term outcomes were analyzed in multiple operationalizations (90th vs 95th percentile, continuous vs categorical, lowest vs average BP) without adjustment for multiplicity, and the highlighted significant SBP>90th percentile result appears selected from this set.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Our a priori primary short-term outcome was severe AKI any time during the hospitalization." ... "For purposes of analysis in the regression models, we focus only on the 90th percentile values."

overall_summary: Although randomization, blinding and analysis of the trial were sound and short-term AKI outcomes were near-complete, the 22-26 month kidney outcomes had extensive and differential missing data (eGFR ~36%, BP ~53% of randomized infants; BP ascertainment differed by arm, P=.044, and loss to follow-up 3.2% vs 8.3%, P=.01), which the authors acknowledge could have produced the single positive SBP finding. Combined with non-gold-standard outcome measurement and multiple outcome operationalizations, the overall risk of bias is high (driven by missing outcome data), particularly for the long-term outcomes.

design_rationale: Patients with isolated coronary vessel disease were explicitly randomly allocated to erythropoietin or control using computer-generated randomization tables ("A custom simple application running in Windows XP ... was used to obtain randomization tables, and the next value of the table was kept secret until a suitable patient was enrolled"), so RoB 2 applies.

domain_judgments.rationale: A computer-generated sequence with some attempt at concealment is described, and baseline data were entered before allocation was known, but the concealment mechanism is vague (no sealed envelopes/central allocation) and there is a notable two-fold baseline imbalance in COPD (32.1% vs 16.5%, P=.079) that is larger than expected by chance in a trial of this size.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "A custom simple application running in Windows XP (Microsoft Corp, Redmond, WA) was used to obtain randomization tables, and the next value of the table was kept secret until a suitable patient was enrolled."

domain_judgments.rationale: This was an open-label trial with no placebo, so patients and the treating ward team were aware of allocation and could have altered co-interventions (notably transfusion practice), although a uniform Hb<8 g/dL transfusion trigger was applied to both groups and all randomized patients (including 3 converted to on-pump) were analyzed by intention-to-treat.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The control group received no treatment... The patients, nurses, and ward physician knew whether HRE was being administered or not, but the investigators did not."

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data appear essentially complete: denominators in the results (158 HRE, 162 control) match the randomized numbers, no post-randomization withdrawals or losses to follow-up are reported, and the primary transfusion outcome was abstracted from clinical records for all patients.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Of the remaining 320 patients, 158 were allocated to HRE administration and all received the intended treatment; 162 were allocated to the control group... These patients were considered as intention-to-treat and were therefore included in the analysis."

domain_judgments.rationale: The outcomes (transfused units, Hb) are objective, laboratory/record-based and measured identically in both arms with a protocolized transfusion trigger, but the decision to transfuse was made by unblinded ward clinicians who knew allocation and the reported secondary trigger ("venous saturation <50%") introduces a subjective element not stated in the Methods.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Transfusion need was triggered by Hb levels less than 8.0 g/dL, and the same criteria were applied to both groups. Hb values were automatically collected by the central laboratory computer."

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary and secondary end points and a power calculation were pre-specified, but no trial registration or protocol is cited, multiple tests were applied "as needed" to each comparison, dozens of adverse-event outcomes were tested without adjustment, and post hoc subgroup analyses (baseline Hb <10.5 and <9 g/dL) favourable to the intervention were reported, indicating scope for selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Every comparison was tested with several statistical techniques (Student t test, univariate regression, Yates' continuity-corrected chi-square test as needed) as appropriate."

overall_summary: This adequately powered, computer-randomized, intention-to-treat trial with complete outcome data and a uniform transfusion trigger raises some concerns rather than high risk: the open-label, no-placebo design meant patients and treating clinicians (who decided on transfusion) knew allocation, allocation concealment is only vaguely described with a notable COPD baseline imbalance, and the absence of a registered protocol alongside multiple statistical tests and post hoc subgroup analyses leaves scope for selective reporting. No single domain reached 'high', so the overall judgment is 'some concerns'.

design_rationale: Explicit random allocation is described: "Randomization was stratified by site and entailed use of computer-generated random numbers," with 650 patients assigned to rHuEPO and 652 to placebo in a prospective, double-blind, placebo-controlled multicenter trial.

domain_judgments.rationale: A computer-generated, site-stratified sequence administered centrally by an independent data coordinating center with an identical-appearing placebo implies adequate generation and concealment, and the large baseline table shows groups "generally comparable," with the few significant differences (iron, transferrin saturation) plausibly due to multiple testing and adjusted for in multivariate analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Randomization was stratified by site and entailed use of computer-generated random numbers"; "Randomization and data analysis were done by the data coordinating center."

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants, caregivers (including the physicians deciding on transfusion) and investigators were blinded by an identical placebo, a common transfusion guideline was applied, pretransfusion hemoglobin levels were nearly identical between arms indicating no differential co-intervention, and analysis was intention-to-treat.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Study drug (40000 units of rHuEPO ... ) or a placebo identical in appearance was administered by subcutaneous injection"; "Analysis of outcomes was on an intent-to-treat basis."

domain_judgments.rationale: All 1302 randomized patients were included in the primary analysis and two opposite worst/best-case imputation analyses for withdrawals gave essentially identical effect estimates (OR 0.67 vs 0.66), indicating results are not biased by the small amount of missing data.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Patients not receiving transfusion at the time of study withdrawal or lost to follow-up were considered not transfused for this analysis. In addition, a second analysis was done in which all patients withdrawn or lost to follow-up were considered transfused."

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes (receipt of transfusion, units transfused, hemoglobin, mortality) are objective and were recorded identically in both arms under double-blind conditions; although the transfusion decision was at physician discretion, assessors/clinicians were blinded to allocation and pretransfusion thresholds were equivalent across groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The primary efficacy end point was transfusion independence, assessed by comparing the percentage of patients in each treatment group who received any RBC transfusion between study days 1 and 28."

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary and secondary end points were prospectively specified in the protocol and analysed as stated, but no pre-registration/protocol is publicly cited, several subgroup analyses and multiple operationalizations of transfusion burden (units per patient, units per day alive) were post hoc, and the manufacturer sponsor designed-review involvement adds concern about selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Although these subgroups were not prospectively identified, they were identified prior to knowledge of treatment assignment and prior to the locking of the database"; "Funding/Support: This study was supported by Ortho Biotech Products LP, manufacturer of rHuEPO ... The final manuscript was reviewed by the study sponsor."

overall_summary: This large, multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial used central computer-generated randomization, intention-to-treat analysis, essentially complete follow-up with sensitivity analyses for withdrawals, and objective blinded outcome measurement (all low risk). Overall judgment of "some concerns" is driven solely by Domain 5: the absence of a publicly available pre-registered protocol, post hoc subgroup and multiple transfusion-outcome operationalizations, and the manufacturer's sponsorship/review of the manuscript raise the possibility of selective reporting.

design_rationale: The EARLYARF trial explicitly states patients were "allocated to EPO or placebo (normal saline) groups in a 1:1 ratio, using a predefined computer-generated randomization sequence with permuted blocks stratified on center" in a prospective, double-blind, placebo-controlled parallel-group design.

domain_judgments.rationale: A computer-generated, block-randomized, centre-stratified sequence with pharmacy-based allocation concealment and identical syringes was used; the observed baseline imbalances (age, sepsis, neurological diagnoses, AKI at randomization) are modest, non-significant for most comparisons, acknowledged by the authors as chance findings, and covariate adjustment did not alter the result.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Eligible patients were allocated to EPO or placebo (normal saline) groups in a 1:1 ratio, using a predefined computer-generated randomization sequence with permuted blocks stratified on center. Concealment was by pharmacist; pairs of identical 5-ml syringes containing EPO (50 000 U in 3 ml) or normal saline were prepared and stored."

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants, clinicians and investigators were blinded to the identical-appearing study syringes, all randomized patients received at least one dose, and the primary analysis was intention-to-treat (with a concordant per-protocol analysis).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Patients, all medical staff, and investigators were masked to treatment." / "The primary outcome and safety endpoints were evaluated in the ITT population... As all randomized patients had received at least one dose of the study medication; the ITT and safety populations were identical."

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary ITT analysis apparently included all 162 randomized patients (one withdrew consent for data), but ~18% lacked the ≥96 h of creatinine sampling needed for a full RAVC (largely due to early death/ICU discharge) and the paper does not explain how RAVC was handled for these patients; longer-term creatinine data were substantially incomplete, though PP and ITT results were concordant.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "PP patients received both doses of study medication, needed at least 96 h for RAVC calculations, and thus, follow-up of at least four post-randomization pCr samples." (ITT n=78/84 vs PP n=63/70; "Plasma creatinine at 90 days (mg/dl) [n] 0.95 (0.79–1.10) [47] 0.85 (0.74–1.07) [56]")

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome was an objective, laboratory-based creatinine metric (RAVC) measured identically in both arms by standardized assays, with outcome assessors blinded until all follow-up and adverse-event recording were complete; baseline creatinine rules were also fixed before unmasking.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Urine GGT, AP and creatinine, and pCr were assayed immediately. Creatinine concentrations were determined by the Jaffe Reaction... Unmasking followed recording of the final AEs of the patient last enrolled."

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered (ACTRN012606000058572) with a pre-specified primary outcome and secondary outcomes defined before unmasking, but numerous outcome operationalizations and multiple post-hoc analyses (e.g., the not-AKI-at-randomization subgroup, alternative baseline-creatinine definitions, adjustment for imbalanced covariates) were reported without evident correction, and protocol details are not available for verification.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The prospectively defined primary outcome was the RAVC..." / "Secondary outcomes, defined before unmasking, included RIFLE... and AKIN... categorical definitions of AKI, plasma cystatin-C, urine output, need for dialysis, death within 7, 30 or 90 days." / "In the subgroup of randomized patients who did not have AKI on randomization (n = 104)... As the study was not powered for such a subgroup analysis, this result must be viewed with caution."

overall_summary: Allocation, blinding and objective laboratory outcome assessment were well handled (D1, D2, D4 low), but the overall rating is "some concerns" because of incompletely explained missing creatinine follow-up for the RAVC primary outcome in ~18% of randomized patients (D3) and multiple post-hoc/unadjusted secondary and subgroup analyses alongside several outcome operationalizations (D5). These issues are unlikely to overturn the main null finding, which was robust across ITT, per-protocol, and covariate-adjusted analyses.

design_rationale: Explicit random allocation is described: "Eligible patients were allocated to EPO ... or standard preventive protocol only in a 1:1 ratio, using a permuted block randomization," with trial registration (NCT01364402) and a prospective RCT design.

domain_judgments.rationale: A permuted-block randomization sequence with 1:1 allocation and central randomization was used, participants were blinded to assignment, and the extensive baseline table (age, sex, weight, BP, SCr, albumin, haemoglobin, eGFR, comorbidity, ACE-inhibitor use) shows no differences beyond chance (all P ≥ 0.11).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Eligible patients were allocated to EPO ... or standard preventive protocol only in a 1:1 ratio, using a permuted block randomization. The patients and the interventional cardiologist were blinded to treatment assignment." ... "The validity of our study is strengthened by use of double blinding and central randomization."

domain_judgments.rationale: Patients and the interventional cardiologist were blinded and the control group received a matching saline bolus; co-interventions (hydration, NAC, atorvastatin 80 mg) were protocolized and delivered equally, with comparable hydration volumes and contrast doses, and all 138 randomized patients appear in the primary analysis (72 vs 66).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Patients in the control group received a bolus of saline only." ... "Atorvastatin 80 mg was started on the day of admission, prior to angiography, and given routinely to all patients throughout their hospital stay."

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome (CIN by serum creatinine) appears available for all 138 randomized patients, but the secondary biomarker outcomes were missing in 40/138 (29%) patients, with the claim of balance ("split equally") asserted without supporting numbers or sensitivity analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "In the current study, our data on NGAL and CC was incomplete in 40 patients, split equally between the EPO and the control group. We therefore believe that our results were not affected by the missing data."

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome is an objective laboratory measure (≥0.5 mg/dL rise in serum creatinine at 24 and 48 h) obtained identically in both arms under double-blind conditions, so assessor knowledge of allocation is very unlikely to have influenced measurement.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "CIN was defined as an increase in serum creatinine of at least 0.5 mg/dL during the first 2 days after exposure to contrast media." ... "Scr post CA was measured at 24 and 48 h post-procedure."

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered (NCT01364402) with a pre-specified primary endpoint, sample-size calculation and biomarker secondary endpoints, but the published report does not state that analyses followed a pre-specified plan, the enrolled sample (138) fell short of the planned 142 after a markedly longer-than-anticipated recruitment period (2011–2015, suggesting possible early stopping), and the acknowledged variability in CIN definitions leaves scope for selection among outcome operationalizations.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The cut-off increase in SCr defining CIN differs in various studies (from 20 to 50% increase, or in absolute values from 0.5 to 1 mg/dL) ... In the time we designed our study, most of the studies defined CIN by a rise of at least 0.5 mg/dL, and in order to be able to compare our results to other studies, we used a similar definition."

overall_summary: This double-blind, centrally randomized, registered trial has low risk for the randomization process, intervention delivery and outcome measurement (objective creatinine-based CIN), but raises some concerns from 29% missing biomarker data addressed only by an unsupported assertion of balance, and from incomplete reporting of adherence to a pre-specified analysis plan alongside recruitment that ended slightly below the planned sample size. Overall risk is therefore "some concerns," driven by domains 3 and 5; the trial was also clearly underpowered given the far lower-than-expected CIN incidence (8.7% vs 44% assumed).

design_rationale: The paper explicitly describes a multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial in which 182 CABG patients were "registered centrally, stratified by center, and randomized before scheduled operation ... on the basis of a computer-generated randomization code."

domain_judgments.rationale: A computer-generated sequence with central registration/stratification by center implies adequate generation and concealment, and the three groups were closely balanced on all demographic, hematologic, and iron-store baseline variables ("There were no significant differences between the three treatment groups in regard to any of the demographic or baseline variables").
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Patients were registered centrally, stratified by center, and randomized before scheduled operation to receive either Epoetin alfa or placebo on the basis of a computer-generated randomization code."

domain_judgments.rationale: Transfusion outcome data were available for ~94% of randomized patients with balanced, mostly explicable exclusions (chiefly 9 patients who never had the operation and so could not be transfused), and an intent-to-treat analysis gave essentially identical results (p=0.054 vs 0.068).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Of those, 171 (94.0%; 59 = 300 IU/kg Epoetin alfa, 60 = 150 IU/kg Epoetin alfa, and 52 = placebo) were evaluable for efficacy... There were no significant differences between treatment groups in the proportion of patients evaluable for efficacy."

domain_judgments.rationale: Transfusion exposure/units and laboratory hematologic measures are objective and recorded identically across groups, but the decision to transfuse is clinician-dependent ("unless clinically indicated") and investigators were not blinded to injection volume, leaving some possibility of influence; multicenter variation in transfusion practice adds further concern.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The investigators used a policy not to transfuse patients with an HCT value greater than 24% after CABG unless clinically indicated."

domain_judgments.rationale: Although double-blind and supported by an intent-to-treat confirmatory analysis, the unblinded injection volume could have revealed dose group to investigators, which matters because the primary outcome (transfusion) is clinician-driven despite a stated HCT <24% transfusion policy; the primary efficacy analysis was also restricted to "evaluable patients" (those operated on and receiving ≥7 doses), excluding randomized patients.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Identity of study medication was blinded, but the volume administered was not blinded to the investigators."

domain_judgments.rationale: A pre-specified primary efficacy variable and analysis plan are described (a strength), but there is no accessible protocol/registration (pre-registration was not customary in 1988–1990), numerous secondary hematologic and safety outcomes were analyzed without multiplicity adjustment, and a post hoc retrospective subgroup analysis by sex is reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Pairwise tests were performed only if there was an overall significant difference between treatment groups. No further adjustments for multiple comparisons were made."

overall_summary: This multicenter, computer-randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial had sound allocation and near-complete outcome data with a confirmatory intent-to-treat analysis, but partial unblinding of investigators (injection volume), a clinician-dependent primary outcome (transfusion decision), use of an "evaluable patient" primary analysis set, and unregistered/unadjusted multiple secondary and post hoc subgroup analyses raise some concerns. No single domain reached high risk, so the overall judgment is "some concerns."

design_rationale: The paper reports a prospective single-blind randomized controlled trial in which 600 eligible cardiac surgery patients were allocated 1:1 to erythropoietin or control using a permuted block randomization scheme performed by a study coordinator (registered NCT01265680).

domain_judgments.rationale: A permuted block sequence was generated and administered by an independent coordinator with allocation concealed from investigators, and baseline characteristics were well balanced across ~25 prognostic variables (only minor differences in CPB and cross-clamp times, plausibly chance in a large table).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "A permuted block randomization scheme with 1:1 allocation was used to keep the group sizes equal. Randomization was performed by a study coordinator immediately after consent was obtained but group assignments were not disclosed to the investigators until the study was complete."

domain_judgments.rationale: Care providers and outcome assessors were blinded and analysis was intention-to-treat with a strict non-discretionary transfusion trigger, but there was no placebo injection so patients were aware of receiving (or not receiving) a subcutaneous bolus, and no data on protocol adherence/co-interventions (e.g., iron compliance) are reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "All investigators, surgeons, anesthesiologists, perfusionists, and intensive care unit physicians responsible for the administration of blood products or involved in the evaluation of outcomes were blinded with respect to group assignment thereby creating a single-blinded study."

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for essentially all randomized participants with no loss to follow-up, and analyses were intention-to-treat.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Of the remaining 600 patients, 300 were allocated to and received HRE and 300 were allocated to the control group... None of the survivors were lost to follow-up."

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome (transfusion incidence) is objective, measured identically in both arms under a strict protocolized transfusion trigger, and the clinicians deciding on transfusion were blinded to allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "A trigger Hb level of 8.0 g/dL was strictly observed as threshold for transfusions allowing no discretion to physicians."

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered with clearly pre-specified primary and secondary endpoints and a priori power calculations, but the emphasis on post hoc stratified/subgroup analyses by baseline Hb and CPB time (which drive the headline conclusion restricting benefit to Hb <13 g/dL) does not appear pre-specified.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The primary endpoint was the incidence of perioperative aRBCt. The secondary endpoints were mortality and the incidence of adverse events in the first 45 days after surgery, Hb level on Postoperative Day 4, and number of units of RBC transfusions..."

overall_summary: This registered, adequately powered RCT used block randomization with concealed allocation, complete follow-up, and an objective, protocol-driven primary outcome assessed by blinded clinicians, yielding low risk in D1, D3 and D4. Overall risk is "some concerns" because of the absence of a placebo (patients unblinded, no adherence data) and reliance on apparently post hoc subgroup/stratified analyses for key conclusions.

design_rationale: The EPICURE trial explicitly used a computer-generated 1:1 randomisation schema, stratified by access route, with double-blind placebo control.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation sequence was computer-generated and handled by an uninvolved technician (suggesting concealment), but a statistically significant baseline imbalance in the key prognostic variable (haemoglobin) raises some concern, and the exact concealment mechanism (e.g., sealed envelopes/central allocation) is not described.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Patients were assigned to receive EPO (+iron) or placebo using a computer-generated randomisation schema in a 1:1 ratio, stratified by planned route... Randomisation was performed by a technician who was not otherwise involved in the study." / "The two groups were well balanced except for the haemoglobin concentration at randomisation which was lower in the EPO group (10.7±1.2 vs. 11.3±1.1 g/dl, p=0.011)."

domain_judgments.rationale: Double-blind design with careful measures to maintain patient and investigator blinding, near-complete adherence (one partial dose), protocolised transfusion triggers, and analysis of all randomised patients who underwent TAVI.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The intravenous tubing used for administering the iron (or placebo) was covered with a drape to guarantee that the patient could not see the infusion solution... The investigator was not present during the infusion to ensure the blindness of treatment allocation." / "All patients received the complete dose of the assigned therapy except for one patient included in the EPO group who refused the second dose of treatment."

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome (RC transfusion) is objective, protocol-triggered, identically ascertained in both arms, independently verified by a blinded blood bank, and outcome assessors were blinded.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Data regarding RC transfusions were further confirmed using the data from the local blood bank (Héma-Québec, Canada), which was blinded regarding treatment groups." / "Treatment assignments were concealed from the investigators gathering data and assessing outcome and safety events until the study was complete."

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for all 100 analysed patients with no loss to follow-up; only 4/104 randomised patients were excluded post-randomisation for reasons (no TAVI performed, pre-procedural bleeding) that are balanced and unlikely to bias results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Patients were followed for 30 days and no patients were lost at follow-up." / "Two patients receiving EPO and one patient receiving placebo infusions did not finally undergo TAVI and were excluded from the analyses. One additional patient was excluded due to active bleeding before TAVI."

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered with a clearly pre-specified primary outcome and sample size, but the covariate-adjusted analysis appears to have been added post hoc in response to the observed haemoglobin imbalance, and multiple unplanned landmark/subgroup analyses are reported without a stated pre-specified analysis plan.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT02390102" / "This lack of association between EPO and transfusion persisted when a landmark analysis with a cut-off at 1 day and 7 days... was performed."

overall_summary: This registered, double-blind, placebo-controlled randomised trial had strong blinding, complete follow-up, and objective blinded outcome ascertainment, but a significant baseline haemoglobin imbalance (with incompletely described allocation concealment) and apparently post hoc adjusted/landmark analyses raise some concerns. The overall judgment of "some concerns" is driven by domains 1 and 5.
